newsitem.title: UK: Europe funds bearish on local stocks, bonds - Merrill. [CORRECTED 12:16 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Europe funds bearish on local stocks, bonds - Merrill. [CORRECTED 12:16 GMT]

text.p: Continental European fund managers will seek to sell European bonds and, to a much lesser degree, equities after the Socialist election win in France, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.

The survey, which covered 67 institutions managing $508 billion, found that sellers of equities will outnumber buyers by one percent. European fund managers are very negative on European bonds, with sellers outnumbering buyers by 25 percent.
It was the first time since the survey began in 1994 that managers were bearish on both European stocks and bonds.

"Hopes of a round of Anglo-Saxon style corporate restructurings in France appear to have been dashed and the whole issue of the nature and timing of European Monetary Union is back in the balance," the survey said.
Almost all of the fund managers in the survey expect EMU to go ahead on time, but 76 percent now expect a soft Euro, up from 38 (corrects figure from 61) percent in May.
France has taken a tremendous fall in popularity; it is now the least favourite equity market in the survey, down from second in May.
UK and Japanese equities both grew in popularity in June.
The survey was carried out by Gallup between the 2nd and 4th of June. -- James Saft, London newsroom +171 542 2734
